records.name: Head of the Schuylkill Regatta Volunteers
records.summary: The volunteer crew behind Philadelphia's Head of the Schuylkill Regatta, a rowing race on the Schuylkill River that has run for more than 56 years. Volunteers help with timing, docks, registration, parking and more.
records.what_you_do: Work half day shifts around lunchtime in one of about a dozen roles: timing, docks, registration, parking, hospitality, information, awards, golf carts, logistics, photography, zero waste and boat launches. Timing needs no rowing or timing experience, and training is provided.

schedule.text: Shifts run in half days split around lunchtime on regatta weekend each fall. Most area prep meetings are held on Zoom.

locations.label: Schuylkill River regatta course, near Boathouse Row

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteers.

first_step.how: Sign up for a shift on the SignUpGenius form linked from the volunteer page, then a Captain confirms your shift and where to report. New volunteers can also attend the all-area volunteer information session on Zoom on Tuesday, October 20, 2026; it is recorded for anyone who misses it.
first_step.basis: The page welcomes new volunteers, says timing needs no rowing experience, provides training, and gives clear steps to start: a shift sign-up and an email contact.
first_step.what_to_expect: A shift lasts about half a day and is split around lunchtime. The work takes place around the regatta course, and the docks role is hands-on. Timing volunteers get training. No fee is listed.
first_visit_tips: Ask volunteers@hosr.org how volunteers get to the course. On race day only vehicles with an HOSR vehicle ID tag can drive onto Kelly Drive, and other traffic uses paid off-site lots with shuttle buses.

Learn where to report misconduct, which the page asks every volunteer to know. Adult volunteers who will not work with minor athletes are encouraged to take the U.S. Center for SafeSport's brief course.
Launch roles need boating experience, and golf cart drivers must be 18 with a driver's license.

records.notes: The venue and parking page (hosr.org/venue-parking/) returned 404, so no SEPTA line or stop is named and access.notes is omitted. The /faq page is the competitor FAQ; only its race-day traffic rule is used, and it is written for spectators and competitors, so the volunteer parking plan should be confirmed by email. Tier 1 had the October 20 information session in schedule text and days [tue]; it is a one time event, so it moved to first_step and days were removed. last_sign_of_life 2026-10 comes from the October 24 and 25, 2026 regatta dates on the homepage. The volunteer page does not say what to wear or where shifts check in. The minimum age of 18 applies only to golf cart drivers, so audience.min_age is omitted.
